1.
Leave granted.
2.
This is a case where the appellant is aggrieved
by  the  order  dated  12.09.2014  passed  by  the  High
Court in Writ Petition No. 1684 of 2014.
3.
In the nature of the order we propose to pass in
this case, we have to necessarily refrain ourselves
from any discussion on merits.  Suffice only to note
that, among other things, the High Court has noted
the  fact  that  the  appellant  had  not  availed  the

statutory remedy open to them before the Sales Tax
Tribunal.
4.
In the nature of the dispute, we are of the view
that  it  will  be  just  and  equitable  to  grant  that
opportunity  to  the  appellant,  having  heard  the
learned counsel appearing for the State as well.
5.
Accordingly, the appeal is partly allowed.  The
impugned  Judgment  of  the  High  Court  is  set  aside.
The  appellant  is  granted  a  period  of  30  days  to
challenge  the  orders  by  filing  a  statutory  appeal
before the Tribunal.  In the event of such an appeal
being  filed,  the  same  shall  be  entertained  by  the
Tribunal as having been filed in time.
6.
We make it clear that we have not considered the
matter on merits and it will be open to both sides to
raise all available contentions before the Tribunal.
